description: We are Kepler's Team, a team of enthusiastic innovators united by a spirit of collaboration, a passion for space and science, and a love of technology. Each of us brings a different skill and perspective, and together we believe that curiosity, teamwork, and creativity can turn NASA’s open data into solutions that matter. Inspired by the mission to explore and understand, we’re here to learn, build, and aim for the stars.
summary:
Postcards from the Moon reimagines the Apollo 11 mission as an interactive journey through one of humanity’s greatest achievements, designed to spark curiosity in school-age space enthusiasts.
Rather than relying on conventional timelines and information-heavy pages, we created an immersive, first-person story that puts visitors at the heart of the mission. Guided by Luna, a friendly robot companion, players follow a mysterious postcard to the Moon, navigate its lunar landscape, and arrive at the historic Sea of Tranquility. There, they uncover the story of the first Moon landing through archival photographs, fascinating discoveries, and hands-on exploration of the scientific instruments left on the surface.
Our project bridges the gap between learning about space exploration and experiencing it. By combining storytelling, interactive 3D visualisation, and accessible scientific explanations, we make the engineering behind Apollo 11 tangible and exciting. Our goal is to turn young learners’ curiosity into exploration, and to inspire a deeper appreciation for the science, innovation, and ambition that made reaching the Moon possible.
details:
1. What does your project do and how does it work?

Our project is an interactive, multi-page website that transforms the Apollo 11 mission into a visual storytelling experience through animations, informative content, interactive navigation and audio.

2. What benefits does your project have?

It makes space exploration engaging and easier to understand, especially for young learners, by combining historical facts with visual storytelling and interactive learning.

3. What is the intended impact of your project?

We aim to inspire curiosity about space exploration and STEM fields while helping people appreciate the science, teamwork and technology behind humanity's first Moon landing.

4. What tools, coding languages, hardware or software did you use?

  • HTML, CSS and JavaScript: Website development and interactivity.
  • GitHub and GitHub Pages: Code management and website hosting.
  • Canva and Figma: Graphics and UI/UX design.
  • ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini: AI-assisted creative development.
  • GIFs and Audio: Visual and immersive storytelling.
  • Code Editor and Browser: Development and testing.

5. How is your project creative?

We present a historic space mission as an interactive journey rather than a conventional information website, combining animations, custom sprites, audio, 3D visuals and AI-assisted creative assets.

6. What factors did your team consider?

  • Historical accuracy and reliability.
  • Simple and intuitive navigation.
  • Engaging visual storytelling.
  • Accessibility and educational value.
  • Technical feasibility.
  • Creativity and user engagement.
  • Consistent design across webpages.
